Description:
Reinvent delivery reliability with predictive AI and multilingual, automated customer care—voice first, text second.

Valio Aimo® serves 20,000+ professional kitchens. Today, missing items are often discovered at delivery or via next-morning manual calls—too late. At Junction 2025, we seek a multimodal AI solution (voice + text + image/video) that turns disruptions into proactive customer experiences and materially reduces operational workload.
Currently, when an ordered product is unavailable, customers only discover it at delivery or via a manual call the next day—too late. The goal is to automate the incomplete delivery process end-to-end.

Your challenge:

1. Pre-picking prediction – Use order, stock, and supplier/quality data to forecast which items are likely to be missing.

2. Proactive notice during picking – If a shortage is detected, an AI agent contacts the customer (call/text) in their language, proposes replacements, and confirms changes instantly.

3. Post-delivery remediation – If a shortage still occurs, the AI triggers after-the-fact outreach and arranges corrective delivery (same-day add-on run or next-day).

4. Multimodal claims – Explore voice, text, images, and video for handling delivery discrepancies.


Impact: This is not only about reducing manual work, but about saving an entire operations team’s workload while improving customer satisfaction.
Insights:
Risk model: per-line Out-of-stock probability (features: supplier reliability, quality incidents, seasonality, pick time windows, freshness SLAs, substitution matrix).

Voice-first agent: two-way calling (outbound & inbound), call-reason classification, intents, confirmations, and auditable logs.

Substitution logic: “good-better-best” per SKU based on availability and recipe suitability.

Images/video: detect and score missing items from photos of opened crates; attach a confidence score.
Resources:
Participants will have access to:

- Real-world order and picking data.

- “Mock data” extracts: order history, pick lines (timestamps), stock & availability, exception/quality logs, supplier delivery history.

- Test access to e-commerce / Minun Aimo for context (no separate sandbox).

- Multilingual APIs (ASR/TTS/NLU) and messaging channels (SMS/WhatsApp/email) for voice & text.

- Mentoring: AI, logistics, customer ops + partner coaching on which background data is essential.

Preferred tech: AI agents (voice & chat), predictive models, NLP/NLU, multimodal (image/video), optional routing/slot optimization.
Judging criteria:
Judging:
Feasibility (production-ready architecture)
Completeness of problem coverage (end-to-end)
Quality of AI integration & customer experience
Demonstrated operational impact (FTE savings).


Path to production: strong demos will be considered for real development with Valio Aimo and partners.


Clear guidance to teams:
Show risk model + agent + notification flow + substitution in one demo.

Bonus: photo/video claims + two-way calling (customer calls back → agent resolves).

Description:
Build a multi-agent AI that autonomously minimizes wastewater pumping energy—one of the most critical processes in modern infrastructure—by forecasting inflow, power prices, and flow dynamics in real time.

Every city relies on invisible systems that keep life running—and wastewater management is one of the most critical. Pumps operate nonstop, consuming massive amounts of energy while facing the chaos of inflow, storms, and fluctuating electricity prices. What if these networks could think for themselves? With multi-agent AI, Valmet and HSY invite you to transform static infrastructure into a living system that predicts, adapts, and optimizes wastewater flow in real time.

Wastewater networks operate 24/7 and cannot stop — yet they hide untapped potential for intelligent optimization. Each pumping station must balance constant flow, limited storage, and fluctuating electricity prices while staying resilient to stormwater surges. Traditional automation follows fixed rules and ignores real-time changes and forecasts. Your task is to build a multi-agent AI system where autonomous agents plan pumping according to daily energy prices, coordinate flow between stations, and find the most energy-efficient pumping strategy without violating safety or process constraints. The goal: make one of society’s most critical infrastructure systems self-optimizing.
Insights:
HSY has long period of data from the pumping wastewater 
and storm rain can be nowadays forecasted. Multi-agents
solution can find solution that human can not figure out.

Electricity prices shift by a 15 minute period, while pumps must obey strict flow limits to prevent system failures. HSY holds decades of real wastewater and inflow data—perfect ground truth for AI to learn from. The real challenge is coordination: can multiple autonomous agents, each with their own goals and data streams, discover pumping strategies no human operator could design?

Example suggestion:

One agent could handle short-term energy price forecasting, another could manage storage canal capacity and a third could optimize flow distribution between pumps.
Resources: Participants will have access to HSY’s historical wastewater and inflow datasets—real operational data spanning years of environmental variation. System communication and control will be implemented through the OPC UA protocol, the industrial standard for secure, real-time data exchange. Mentors from Valmet, HSY, and Aalto University will provide hands-on guidance in areas such as process automation, multi-agent architectures, and in future solutions can be tested with digital twin simulation. Teams are free to use any AI framework of their choice—from reinforcement learning environments to optimization libraries or custom-built agent systems.
Judging criteria:
Winning teams will demonstrate how autonomous agents can truly think together—balancing energy efficiency, flow stability, and system safety in real time. Evaluation focuses on technical soundness, creativity of AI coordination, realistic integration with OPC UA and Digital Twin environments, and potential real-world impact on critical infrastructure. Bonus points for solutions that visualize decision-making clearly and show measurable energy savings under variable conditions.

Technical soundness and functionality (25%) – stability, efficiency, and correctness of the AI logic under realistic conditions.


Creativity and AI coordination (25%) – originality in agent interaction, forecasting methods, and adaptive control strategies.


Real-world applicability and integration (25%) – feasibility for deployment using OPC UA, Digital Twin, or similar industrial frameworks.


Clarity and impact demonstration (25%) – how clearly the solution communicates its logic, benefits, and measurable energy savings.
About Company: Valmet Automation and HSY (Helsingin seudun ympäristöpalvelut) join forces to shape the future of smart infrastructure. Valmet Automation provides advanced distributed automation systems used in pulp, paper, and energy industries, while HSY operates Helsinki’s critical water and wastewater networks. Together, they aim to explore how AI and data-driven automation can optimize pumping, reduce energy consumption, and support sustainable urban operations. By taking part in Junction, they invite developers to co-create practical AI solutions that transform industrial and municipal systems into intelligent, self-learning networks.

Challenge name: Reputation Recon: AI-Powered Software Trust Assessment
Description:
Build an AI assessor that turns a product name or URL into a CISO-ready trust brief with sources in minutes.

Security teams and CISOs (Chief Information Security Officer) are constantly asked to approve new tools they’ve never seen before. They need accurate, concise, and source-grounded snapshots of a product’s security posture, fast. This challenge asks participants to build a GenAI-powered assessor that fetches reliable signals from the web and synthesizes them into a decision-ready brief. Help us move security from reactive firefighting to proactive enablement.

Note: Teams may optionally evaluate emerging integration frameworks (e.g., MCP services) as targets of assessment, but MCP is not required.

Given minimal input (product name, vendor, or URL), build a system that:
- Resolves the entity and vendor identity.
- Classifies the software into a clear taxonomy (e.g., File sharing, GenAI tool, SaaS CRM, Endpoint agent).
- Produces a concise security posture summary with citations.
- Covers: description, usage, vendor reputation, CVE trend summaries (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures), incidents/abuse signals, data handling/compliance, deployment/admin controls, and transparent 0–100 trust/risk score with rationale and confidence.
- Suggests 1–2 safer alternatives with short rationale.

Deliverables can be a CLI (Command Line Interface), service, or bonus web UI with compare-view. A lightweight local cache with timestamps and reproducibility is required.
Insights: Focus on high-signal sources: vendor security/PSIRT pages (Product Security Incident Response Team), Terms of Service/Data Processing Agreement, (System and Organization Controls Type II), ISO attestations, reputable advisories/CERTs (Notices from Computer Emergency Response Teams or vendors), and CISA KEV (CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog). Guard against hallucinations by labeling vendor-stated vs. independent claims. When data is scarce, return “Insufficient public evidence.”
Resources:
Withsecure will provide:

Pre-prepared list of applications (names, optional binary hashes).


Guidance on source prioritization and claim–evidence mapping.


Public references: CVE/CVSS (Common Vulnerability Scoring System) databases, CISA KEV, vendor security pages, disclosure/bug bounty sites.


Example prompts for entity resolution and categorization.


Mentors on-site during the weekend (technical + domain expertise).


Bonus theme: assessing MCP-style integrations.


Required: lightweight local cache (JSON/SQLite), snapshot mode, deterministic parameters.
Judging criteria:
Evaluation criteria: 

Problem-fit and readability; correct entity resolution and categorization; evidence quality; security posture synthesis (trends, incidents, compliance); technical execution and resilience; transparent scoring logic; relevant alternatives with mini-compare.

Functional Requirements
- Minimal Input: Accept product name, vendor, or URL; resolve to canonical product.
- Categorization: Assign at least one category from taxonomy with justification.
- Security Posture: Summarize CVE trends (12–24mo), incidents/abuse, compliance posture, admin controls.
- Trust/Risk Rating: Transparent 0–100 with rationale and confidence.
- Alternatives: Suggest safer tools with short rationale.
- Citations: ≤8 URLs, each mapped to claims.
- Interface: CLI (Command Line Interface) or service; bonus simple compare UI.
- Local Cache: Required with timestamps and reproducibility.


Non-Functional Requirements
- GenAI use: entity resolution, classification, summarization; guard against hallucinations.
- Privacy: no customer PII; label vendor vs independent claims.
- Reproducibility: deterministic prompts, snapshot mode, cached raw fetches.
- Resilience: handle missing data, API rate limits, partial failures gracefully.


Evaluation Rubric (100 pts)
- Problem fit & clarity (15)
- Entity resolution & categorization (20)
- Evidence & citation quality (24)
- Security posture synthesis (12)
- Technical execution & resilience (15)
- Trust/risk score transparency (8)
- Alternatives & quick compare (6)

Winning projects will emphasize clarity: a brief readable in under 2 minutes, ≤8 links, transparent scoring logic, and explicit evidence labeling.

Challenge name: Agentic AI with the flexibility of code and easyness of no-code
Description:
n8n is an open-source workflow automation platform that bridges the gap between no-code simplicity and full-code power. This challenge invites you to harness n8n to build agentic AI systems — intelligent workflows that can reason, decide, and act autonomously across APIs, apps, and data sources.

Your task is to design and implement an AI agent (or multi-agent system) that leverages n8n’s flexibility to perform meaningful real-world tasks — from automating research or customer interactions to coordinating multiple AI tools, APIs, or databases. Combine reasoning models with n8n’s modular workflows to demonstrate what’s possible when code and no-code meet agentic intelligence.

What we’re looking for

Innovative use of AI reasoning or planning inside n8n workflows

Creative integration of multiple APIs, LLMs, or data sources

Strong demonstration of autonomy or real-world usefulness

Bonus points for open-source reusability or showcasing how non-developers could extend your system

Getting Started
You can use n8n Cloud
 or self-host locally. Explore built-in AI nodes or integrate external APIs (OpenAI, Hugging Face, Anthropic, etc.) to create dynamic agentic flows.

The company focuses on empowering developers and technical teams to automate without limits, emphasizing privacy, self-hosting, and long-term scalability. With a global open-source community and an enterprise-grade platform, n8n brings technical depth, connectors, and real-world automation expertise to Junction. Description:
Design an AIxAR experience for Spectacles that transforms AR glasses into an intelligent companion aware of your world, context, and needs.

AR glasses like Spectacles represent the next frontier of personal technology. They see what you see, hear what you hear, and understand the world around you—unlocking new ways for humans and AI to work together in real-time.
